description:
Prove the edit-and-refresh loop returns a repository to agreement, so the
motivating use case of this epic cannot regress unnoticed.

## Background

The profiles MVP made an in-place edit to profile-owned content unrecoverable,
and that is the reason this epic was prioritized. The loop that resolves it
works today, verified against a built binary: editing a profile-owned target
makes `jit profile validate` report the profile diverged; `jit profile capture`
over the package's own directory folds the edit into the package; `jit profile
apply` then sees the target's current value equal to the candidate, publishes no
change to it, rewrites the record's package identity and base fingerprints, and
`jit profile validate` reports agreement again. No version bump is involved, and
apply carries no installed-identity precondition, unlike reconfigure.

Each half of that loop has coverage. `test_capture_profile_package_publishes_an_identity_reflecting_an_in_place_edit`
covers capture refreshing from an edit, and
`test_apply_profile_package_reapplies_changed_content_and_rewrites_its_record`
covers apply rewriting a record for a changed package. Nothing joins them, so
nothing observes the property the epic exists to deliver. The loop rests on apply
having no identity gate; reconfigure acquired exactly such a gate deliberately,
so a later change adding one to apply would close the loop again and no test
would fail.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A test edits a profile-owned target in place, refreshes the package from that edit, re-applies, and asserts the repository reports agreement, with each step's observable outcome asserted rather than only the final state.
- [hard] REQ-02: The test asserts the loop requires no package version change, so a re-introduced version or identity precondition on the application path fails it.
- [hard] REQ-03: A test asserts that applying without refreshing the package first refuses the target, writes nothing, and leaves the edit intact.
- [hard] REQ-04: The suite is a module of an existing integration-test target.
title: Prove an in-place edit refreshes back into agreement
